name: Demas
charge: Forsaking Paul, having loved this present world
summary: Three times Demas appears in Paul's letters: a fellowlabourer sending greetings from Rome, then a name without a word, then a name with a verdict. Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica. Scripture says nothing more of him.
offense: He had stood with Paul in the first imprisonment, named with Luke among the fellowlabourers. In the second, with Paul's death near, he loved this present world and went to Thessalonica. The love of the world is named by John as the thing that cannot share a heart with the love of the Father.
judgment: No sentence is written; the departure is the record. The law's word on the man who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the apostle's on the friendship of the world, stand over the empty place where his name had been. Whether he came back is not told.

lawsResolved.text: Lust and Carnal Nature of Man (section)

text.text: Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me:
For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.
Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you.
There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.
Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.
And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.
Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.
And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
